Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Metal generating Water cross-polarity — precision nourishing and opening intelligence
candidates.k2_overview: Your Metal moves as the Sage: tempered care, nurture with a fine edge of standards. You were shaped by teachings that held you to something, and you shelter others the same way, protection that also sharpens. Knowledge in your keeping stays true. Let some care through unpolished. Warmth needs no proofing.
candidates.k2_functional: You think in tested doctrine: knowledge kept because it held under strikes.

k2_domain_readings.Knowledge: Your knowledge is armory-grade: fewer books, deeply proofed, instantly deployable. You trust what survived testing. Curate hard, and reread the masters yearly. Your edge is depth.
k2_domain_readings.Shelter: Your shelter is a forge-side bench: people come to you and leave straightened. You protect by tempering. Remember some visitors need only warmth. Not everything cracked wants rework.
k2_domain_readings.Nurture: The nourishing thread runs steel-true. Where care came early, you draw on it without thinking. Where it was missing, you set your own standard. Keep the precision, soften the grading.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, shelter comes in small measure. You are drawn to the few places that feel safe and settle deep in them.

angles.drive: Whatever you are told stays with you. Being a safe place is how you know you matter, so you keep a confidence rather than ever use it. People hand you what they have shown no one else, and they leave lighter.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a confidence means carrying it. You hold what people tell you rather than talk it through with anyone, and the weight of other lives sits on your own rest. Some days you walk around full of secrets that are not even yours.
angles.cost_others: You keep your own troubles as closely as everyone else's. You would rather hold things than need holding, and the people who tell you everything hear nothing of yours. Your closest friends see your calm face and never your worries.

angles.drive: You learn a thing properly or not at all. A trusted teacher and a subject that holds still feel like shelter to you, and you stay with both until it is whole. Your knowledge survives hard questions because it runs all the way down.
angles.cost_self: Learning it properly takes you longer. Knowing a thing to its end matters to you more than knowing it well enough, and most chances ask for less. Openings go to quicker people while you are still at chapter three.
angles.cost_others: Teaching waits until you have learned it properly. You would rather pass a subject on whole than in pieces, and the people learning from you get nothing before the whole arrives. Your lessons arrive late but complete, safe ground to build on.

angles.drive: You steady people by holding them to something. Keeping someone safe matters more to you than keeping them comfortable, so your care arrives as a standard rather than a hug. In a storm, others find a fixed point in you.
angles.cost_self: Steadying people earns you respect more than closeness. Being needed when things fall apart suits you more than being phoned for nothing, and the no-reason calls are what you miss. Underneath, you would like to be sought out for your company alone.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone arrives shaken, you offer them the shelter you would want for yourself. Firm ground is what you seek in a bad hour, and you hand on the words that once held you. Your warmth reaches them a step behind your advice.

friction.define: As a friction, shelter piles up around you. Cover feels like safety to you, and you spend years under a roof you have outgrown.

angles.drive: You stay the student long after you were able to teach. Learning under someone suits you more than standing alone, and that keeps your seat in the back row past its use. You need no one's permission to stop being the student.
angles.cost_self: Staying the student keeps you safe and small. You would rather stay under what you are learning than stand on what you know, and staying asks nothing of you. You pass up the place meant for you for one more year of learning.
angles.cost_others: Your door stays closed while you stay the student. You keep learning under someone else's wing instead of spreading your own, and the people who need your shelter wait outside. Each year you remain the student is a year they go without it.

angles.drive: Protective is your instinct with the people you love. You need them safe more than you need them tested, so you step in before letting them fall. You are protecting them from the one thing that would have taught them.
angles.cost_self: Being too protective costs you your sleep. You carry every risk your family should carry themselves, and you choose tired over watching them hurt. You lose your own rest to every risk you take off their hands.
angles.cost_others: Your protective side keeps the ones you love from finding their feet. Catching them matters more to you than letting them learn, and you take one lesson from them with every rescue. You give them safety and take away their own first steps.

angles.drive: You wait to be told before you trust your own read. A word from someone wiser feels like cover, and you keep asking long after you know. You hand your best judgement to people who know less than you do.
angles.cost_self: Waiting to be told leaves your own good sense unused for weeks. You need the one in charge to say it is safe, and their word comes later than your own read did. Your first instinct is often right and seldom acted on.
angles.cost_others: When others look to you for a call, you wait to be told too. You want the shelter of a wiser word first, and the people counting on you wait while you ask. They lose days to a decision you had already reached.

edge.lead: Metal runs through your family, your mind and your health. It is the secret told at home that stops with you, the one subject you study down to its roots, and the old habit that keeps you steady through a hard year.

angles.cost_self: Loving by correcting costs you the ones who stop bringing things. You put being useful to someone ahead of being close to them, and the corrected learn to bring you only finished things. You get respect for it, and the closeness goes somewhere less exact.
angles.cost_others: Correcting is what you give people wanting comfort. You would rather set people straight than let them be, and you send them home taught instead of held. With every correction, you take from them the comfort they came for.

angles.drive: You wait to be told before you trust your own read. A word from someone wiser feels like cover, and you keep asking long after you know. You hand your best judgement to people who know less than you do.
angles.cost_self: Waiting to be told leaves your own good sense unused for weeks. You need someone above you to say it is safe, and their word comes later than your own read did. Your first instinct is often right and seldom acted on.
angles.cost_others: When others look to you for a call, you wait to be told too. You want the shelter of a wiser word first, and the people counting on you wait while you ask. They lose days to a decision you had already reached.

$provenance.replaced: Your door stays closed while you stay the student. You keep your knowledge under another's wing rather than make one of it, and the ones who need your shelter stand outside. Every year as the student, you keep a shelter from people who needed it.
